We did not make this assumption since it was not needed, but should mention that $f_{A,B,C}$, if modular at all, is expected automatically to be modular for a congruence subgroup, because it has a Fourier expansion with integral coefficients in some rational power of $q$ and a standard conjecture says that the Fourier expansion of a modular function on a non-congruence subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbf Z)$ always has unbounded denominators. :::
